extraction.name: PIQA
extraction.description: A benchmark dataset for physical commonsense reasoning, where a model must choose the most sensible solution to a natural-language physical goal. It tests knowledge of everyday objects, their physical properties, affordances, and how they can be manipulated.
extraction.creator: Yonatan Bisk, Rowan Zellers, Ronan Le Bras, Jianfeng Gao, Yejin Choi
extraction.publisher: Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AAAI)
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Annotators were prompted with links to Instructables and asked to glance at the instructions, then construct two component tasks by articulating a physical goal, a valid solution, and an invalid permutation of their own solution.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Instructables.com instructions, a crowdsourced collection of how-to instructions with images/videos and tool lists.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators were prompted with links to Instructables, asked to glance at the instructions and use them as inspiration to construct two component tasks, then articulate a physical goal, a valid solution, and a permutation of their own solution that makes it invalid. The design aimed to encourage out-of-the-box thinking and reduce reporting bias.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Two solution choices per example (a valid solution and an invalid permutation).
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset was designed to reduce reporting bias and spurious artifacts, since annotators otherwise tended to choose prototypical kitchen/garage solutions and common objects. The paper also notes that the dataset is still dominated by small edits between solution pairs.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark is limited to physical commonsense in everyday situations and may not generalize beyond this setting. The paper also notes that many examples are only small edits apart, and that the dataset is challenging to pin down because physical commonsense lacks a rich literature. It is intended for evaluating physical commonsense understanding, not abstract tasks.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper frames the dataset as useful for advancing AI systems and robots that interact with the world and understand natural language, with broader implications for building language representations that capture real-world details.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is for benchmarking and evaluating physical commonsense understanding in multiple-choice question answering. The paper also uses it for training/validation analysis of models such as RoBERTa, and notes it can augment prior work on studying syntax.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: They asked annotators to provide a permutation to their own solution which makes it invalid, often subtly; this was done to assist diversity and to flatten the distribution of referenced objects.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Annotators were prompted with links to Instructables and asked to glance at the instructions, pull out or be inspired by them to construct two component tasks, then articulate the goal and how to achieve it.
